title: Safeguarded version-introduction policy: ramp schedules, probes, and automated egress
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Define and implement a production-ready 'version-introduction' policy engine that controls progressive exposure of new model versions across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. The engine will express ramp schedules, shadow probing, deterministic A/B splits, divergence detection, and automated egress (rollback/fallback) using an auditable DSL. Goals: - Provide operators a compact, composable policy language for multi-step ramps (fractional traffic, time windows, and conditional steps). - Implement guardrails for latency, error-rate, and embedding-quality regressions with configurable thresholds and backoff semantics. - Support 'probe' traffic (shadowed requests with golden comparison) and automated arbitration for ambiguous regressions. - Integrate with Console rollouts UI, telemetry, and the runtime routing layer for fast actuation. Non-goals: - Not addressing model packaging or training pipelines. - Not replacing ad-hoc emergency manual rollbacks during incidents; this augments them.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL v1 implemented and documented with examples for 3-step fractional ramps and A/B splits
Runtime adapter that converts DSL to routing directives (percentage splits, mirror rules) for hosted and dedicated clusters
Automated guardrail executor that evaluates metrics every minute and triggers egress when thresholds are breached
Shadow probe subsystem that records golden comparisons and surfaces divergence rates in Console
End-to-end test harness (simulated traffic + fault injection) with pass/fail gating included in CI
decisions: Use a declarative YAML-first policy DSL that compiles to an intermediate state machine rather than embedding imperative scripts
Guardrail evaluation will be centralized (Console policy-service) and will emit action intents; runtime will be authoritative only for execution to avoid split-brain
Rollback heuristics will combine magnitude (relative metric change), persistence (windowed signal), and impact (user-facing error rate) for higher precision before automatic egress
Shadow probing will use a sampled mirror rate default 5% with configurable golden comparator and difference thresholds per KPI
notes: Prototype RFC submitted: docs/rfcs/version-intro-policy.md (see link below)
We evaluated two approaches for thresholding: fixed percentage vs. CUSUM change detection. Chose CUSUM-like detection for sensitivity to small sustained drifts while avoiding noise-driven rollbacks.
Runtime cost estimates: additional CPU for comparator hooks ~2-3% at 5% mirror rate; KV-cache warming improvements expected to offset latency overhead in dedicated mode.
Security review flagged requirement for audit log enrichment (who/why action) when an automatic egress triggers — added security_review_required flag
